sources.ref: NTA, JEE (Main) 2026 Session 2, B.E./B.Tech question paper 'B Tech 2nd Apr 2026 Shift 1' (English)
NTA, JEE (Main) 2026 Session 2 final answer key of B.E./B.Tech on which result compiled, Exam Date 02.04.2026, Shift First (page 1)

notes: Previous-year questions from NTA's JEE (Main) 2026 paper of 2 April 2026, Shift 1 (B.E./B.Tech), ingested with pyq-ingest. Stems, options, statements and list items keep NTA's English wording exactly; NTA published this paper in English only, so the Hindi is our translation (hi_source: translation) and must be reviewed as such. Answers are NTA's final key (result-compiled, Session 2); our own solutions reach the same answer for every question in this file. Question ids 9001 and up mark ingested PYQs. Review before use: q.phy.electric-charges-fields.dipole.9001 (paper Q36) needs its figure img.electric-charges-fields.pyq-crossed-dipoles, which is requested, not approved; it is mock-only so it never ships in a device bundle without the figure.

stem.en: Two short electric dipoles $A$ and $B$ having dipole moment $p_1$ and $p_2$ respectively are placed with their axis mutually perpendicular as shown in the figure. The resultant electric field at a point $x$ is making an angle of $60^\circ$ with the line joining points $O$ and $x$. The ratio of the dipole moments $\frac{p_2}{p_1}$ is ______.
stem.hi: दो लघु विद्युत द्विध्रुव $A$ और $B$, जिनके द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण क्रमशः $p_1$ और $p_2$ हैं, चित्र में दिखाए अनुसार अपनी अक्षों को परस्पर लंबवत रखकर रखे गए हैं। बिंदु $x$ पर परिणामी विद्युत क्षेत्र $60^\circ$ का कोण बनाता है, बिंदुओं $O$ और $x$ को मिलाने वाली रेखा से। द्विध्रुव आघूर्णों का अनुपात $\frac{p_2}{p_1}$ ______ है।

feynman.en: Point $x$ is on the axis of $A$ but on the perpendicular bisector (equatorial line) of $B$. The axial field is twice as strong per unit moment, and the two fields are at right angles.
feynman.hi: बिंदु $x$, $A$ की अक्ष पर है परंतु $B$ की निरक्षीय रेखा पर। अक्षीय क्षेत्र प्रति एकांक आघूर्ण दोगुना होता है, और दोनों क्षेत्र परस्पर लंबवत हैं।

steps.en: $E_A=\frac{2kp_1}{r^3}$ along the line $Ox$; $E_B=\frac{kp_2}{r^3}$ perpendicular to it.
